title: Jay Shah Reappointed Unopposed as ICC Chair for Second Term
excerpt: The ICC Board confirmed Shah's second term at its Bali meetings. He now leads the game through the 2027 World Cup in Southern Africa and cricket's Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028.
body:
• Jay Shah has been reappointed unopposed as ICC Chair for a second term, confirmed by the ICC Board at its meetings in Bali following a proposal by the ICC directors.
  • His second term covers cricket's return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles 2028 and the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 in Southern Africa.
  • Shah, 38, first took charge on December 1, 2024, after serving as BCCI Honorary Secretary from 2019 to 2024, when the Women's Premier League was launched and pay parity in international match fees was introduced.
  • The ICC's statement did not give an end date for the new term; Cricbuzz reported a three-year term running to December 2030 under the ICC constitution's two-term limit.

Jay Shah will lead world cricket into its Olympic return. The International Cricket Council (ICC) Board has confirmed his unopposed reappointment as Chair for a second term, following a proposal by the ICC directors at the Board meetings in Bali, Indonesia. Shah was the only name in the running, ESPNcricinfo reported.

“We are entering one of the most important and exciting periods in our sport's history. Cricket's return to the Olympic Games at LA28 presents an extraordinary opportunity to introduce our game to new audiences and inspire a new generation of players and fans.”

— Jay Shah, ICC Chair

“I am deeply honoured by the confidence the ICC Board has placed in me,” Shah said in the ICC statement. “Serving as Chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, and I remain committed to working with our Members to advance the interests of cricket across the world.” The ICC said the decision reflects the Board's confidence in his leadership and provides continuity, with global expansion, growth in fandom and commercial development central to its strategic roadmap.

The first term, and the BCCI years before it

Shah assumed charge as ICC Chair in December 2024. In his first term, the ICC Men's Champions Trophy returned in 2025 after an eight-year gap, the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2025 set new benchmarks in attendance and viewership, and the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 was co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka, the BCCI said in its congratulatory release.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=owMFejU5RDQ

Before the ICC, Shah was BCCI Honorary Secretary from 2019 to 2024. The BCCI credited that tenure with the launch of the Women's Premier League, pay parity in international match fees for contracted women cricketers, a Test Cricket Incentive Scheme for senior men, a substantial increase in prize money across domestic tournaments, and the development of the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. India also hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 during his tenure, which the BCCI described as the most attended cricket tournament in history. Shah played a part, as a member of the ICC's Olympics Working Group, in securing cricket's place in the LA28 programme, the BCCI added.

What the Board members said

BCCI President Mithun Manhas said Shah “worked at every level of Indian cricket before taking on the global role, and that grounding shows in how he leads,” adding that the Board's decision “reflects the confidence ICC members have in him.” England and Wales Cricket Board Chair Richard Thompson said continued leadership comes at an important time, with the international calendar, bilateral cricket's relevance and major events all to be protected. ICC Independent Director Dr. Ros Rivaz pointed to the growth of women's cricket and the need to support players whose opportunities have been disrupted. Deputy Chair Tavengwa Mukuhlani, of Zimbabwe Cricket, highlighted the Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 bringing the game to new audiences across Africa.

Other decisions at Bali, and what comes next

The Bali meetings also confirmed that the World Test Championship will remain a nine-team tournament until 2031, that Bangladesh and the USA will host the T20 qualifiers for cricket's Olympic tournament, and that the Super Six stage has been scrapped from the ODI qualifier for the 2027 World Cup, ESPNcricinfo reported. On the term itself, the ICC statement set no end date; Cricbuzz reported that members approved another three-year term, taking Shah to December 2030, and that the ICC constitution allows a chair a maximum of two terms of three years each.

What is not in dispute is the calendar Shah now owns: the ODI World Cup in Southern Africa in 2027, and then Los Angeles 2028, where men's and women's T20 competitions return cricket to the Olympics 128 years after the sport last featured at the Games, as the BCCI put it. For the diaspora, LA28 is the home fixture — cricket's biggest showcase staged in the United States, under an Indian chair.
